description: The postability check a video+copy package has to clear can both pass and bite, on the same three artifacts the entry's historical run_ids name plus the historical 321-char attack: three packages that shipped reproduce their logged acceptance verdicts (960x540/1.778/3.0s, 1280x720/1.778/4.0s, 1080x1080/1.000/2.0s, captions 150/99/148, alt texts 112/99/117), the attack caption is caught at 321, and eight authored controls walk the caption, alt-text, aspect and duration boundaries from the inside to the outside — 280 passes and 281 is caught, empty text is caught, 1000 passes and 1001 is caught, a portrait crop is caught on aspect alone, a 141s clip is caught on duration alone, and a text file passed as a video reaches the probe-fail exit with no poster.
notes: rcos-eval/2: this package declares NO adapter of its own. It names the registered
capability and the input document, and the run reaches the capability through the
invocation kernel — `rcos run x-media-package --input ...` takes the identical path.
The thing being evaluated is the thing reuse will call.
This replaces NOTHING. The two eval entries already on the registry entry
('postable-video-package' and the xcheck audit one) are historical assertions and stay
byte-for-byte as written; this receipt is a new record that links backward by exercising
the SAME checker (capabilities/x-media-package/adapter/xcheck.py, sha256 641ce906…,
pinned in gates/check.js) on the SAME three artifact files the historical logs name,
whose sha256 are pinned in the artifact_identity_pinned gate.
Every historical fact is reproduced, not invented: the three acceptance packages
re-run the checker over evidence/chalk-capture-recipe/eval-2/chalk-eval2.mp4,
evidence/dell-gpu-dispatch/eval-2/rcos-dispatch-eval-2-out.mp4 and
evidence/face-in-scene-shot/eval-2/shot-face-v2-r3.mp4 with the caption/alt text from
evidence/x-media-package/{eval-1,eval-2,eval-3}, and the expected stdout lines are the
lines committed in evidence/x-media-package/{eval-1/xcheck.log, eval-2/xcheck.log,
eval-3.log} — including the printed sizes 0.1MB / 0.0MB / 0.4MB and the two muse poster
verdicts (SHIP) recorded in eval-1/muse-poster.log and muse-poster-e3.log, which is why
the poster artifact is part of what this eval checks rather than a side effect.
The attack package re-runs evidence/x-media-package/attack/caption-long.txt and must
reproduce 'FAIL CAPTION 321 > 280 chars' from attack/long-caption.log.
The eight authored controls have ZERO historical lineage and are labeled as such:
* six boundary texts composed to exact stripped lengths (280/281/1000/1001 and the
two empty files), each verified with the checker's own strip() semantics;
* portrait-crop-chalk.mp4, generated by
ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -i chalk-eval2.mp4 -vf crop=180:540:390:0 -an
-c:v libx264 -preset veryfast -crf 23 -pix_fmt yuv420p portrait-crop-chalk.mp4
(180x540, 3.0s — aspect 0.333 is its only out-of-range fact);
* duration-141s.mp4, generated by
ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -f lavfi -i color=c=black:s=180x320:r=10:d=141 -an
-c:v libx264 -preset veryfast -crf 23 -pix_fmt yuv420p duration-141s.mp4
(180x320, 141.0s — aspect 0.562 is in range, so duration is its only fail line).
The two derived videos were generated on this box by the commands above and pinned by
hash like every other fixture.
Two authoring facts make the gates real rather than decorative:
* the poster is written by the checker BEFORE it decides pass/fail, so failing
packages still carry a poster (as the historical attack log shows) and only the
probe-failure exit (4) carries none;
* re-extracting the poster twice with identical ffmpeg arguments produces
byte-identical JPEGs, and not merely against itself: measured on this box, the fresh
extraction reproduces the committed historical x-poster.jpg byte-for-byte on all
three acceptance videos (sha 7b73e1ca… / f7aff2b0… / 18830a2c…, pinned in
poster_offset_reproduced), so each receipt describes the very poster artifact the
muse poster gates shipped and the gate can FALSIFY a wrong seek or a wrong source
instead of rubber-stamping whatever the run recorded.
The seek parity matters for one package: the checker asks for str(min(1.0, dur/3)) in
python and the adapter mirrors it in node; the double 2/3 prints as
0.6666666666666666 in both runtimes, which the 2.0s slate package exercises.
Pins are metadata, not measurements: dimensions, durations, printable sizes and
character counts are exact (the checker prints them from ffprobe and len(), not from a
measurement on this box); the poster bytes are pinned by the sha256 the run recorded
and re-derived independently by the offset gate. Packages run in per-package scratch
directories under the work dir, so the eight packages sharing chalk-eval2.mp4 do not
race for one x-poster.jpg and no frozen input is ever written through.
